findings.evidence: Container: toast. Placement: in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks.
findings.fix: Present this message in a persistent modal or inline block that stays until dismissed, not a self-clearing toast, matching the blocking severity of an expired reset link.
findings.violation: The underlying problem is fully blocking (the reader cannot proceed with password reset at all on an expired link, and the dialog description confirms it blocks the new-password field), yet the container is annotated as a self-clearing toast, so a reader who looks away misses the one message explaining why they cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again.
findings.fix: Add a brief reason for the limit, e.g. "This field takes a maximum of 30 characters to fit the shipping label. Shorten the entry and save again."
findings.violation: States a length restriction the reader will meet again with no reason attached, and knowing the reason (why 30 characters) would help the reader avoid retyping an over-length entry next time.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Add a brief acknowledgment before the referral, e.g. "We're sorry, your last changes were not saved and can't be recovered. Contact support and we'll help you redo them."
findings.violation: Reports a completed, unrecoverable loss as a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what the loss means for the reader; 'Suggested fix: none' and no other message on this screen offers a way forward beyond the contact-support referral already in the text.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read.
findings.fix: Validate the file's format as soon as it is selected and show this message immediately, before the reader reaches submit.
findings.violation: Predictable mistake is yes and the message fires on-submit with no earlier warning, yet file format is a property the product can already read from the selected file before the reader submits, so this foreseeable mismatch could have been caught at file selection rather than only on submit.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page
findings.fix: Move the message to directly below the new-password field, alongside the other field-level messages on this screen.
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a long form rather than beside or below the password field it concerns, requiring the reader to scroll up to find it even though the field itself stays on screen.
